description: A structured finance director must authorize the sale of a $12,000,000 receivables pool to an institutional buyer and finalize the price, recourse, reserve, remittance, and compliance conditions, with input from legal, credit risk, servicing operations, and financial crime compliance.

shared_context.S1: The bank has assembled a $12,000,000 pool of commercial receivables for a proposed sale to Meridian Receivables Fund.
shared_context.S2: The buyer's draft proposal offers $11,700,000 and requests customary seller support for collection shortfalls.
shared_context.S3: Elena has authority to authorize the transaction and set its closing conditions.
shared_context.S4: The bank's pre-closing routine is a cross-functional review in which legal, credit risk, servicing operations, and financial crime compliance each report unresolved items before the final authorization.

PF1.text: Martin confirmed in buyer's counsel's email this morning that Meridian will pay exactly $11,400,000 only for a non-recourse true sale; any seller guarantee of collection shortfalls would invalidate the agreed structure. The email has not yet been attached to the transaction file.

PF2.text: Aisha found while reviewing the debtor tape this week that the largest obligor represents 18% of the pool, above the bank's 10% single-obligor threshold; credit policy therefore requires a $1,200,000 first-loss reserve before closing. Her revised concentration worksheet is not yet in the risk system.

PF3.text: Jon confirmed with the lockbox bank this morning that collections can be redirected on June 15, 2026, but only if the transaction includes a lockbox activation commitment effective on that date. The confirmation is still in his operations email and has not been circulated.

PF4.text: Nadia completed a file review this week and found that one beneficial owner of a pool debtor requires enhanced sanctions screening before closing, with the result to be documented within two business days after completion. The updated screening instruction has not yet been added to the closing checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The receivables sale must be authorized at a purchase price of exactly $11,400,000.
The transaction must be structured without recourse to the seller.
A first-loss reserve of exactly $1,200,000 must be established.
The settlement must include a lockbox activation commitment effective June 15, 2026.
Enhanced sanctions screening must be required before closing.
Screening documentation must be due within exactly two business days after completion.
The transaction must include a commitment to complete the enhanced screening before closing.

content_checks.C6: any('lockbox activation commitment' in c['detail'] and ('June 15, 2026' in c['detail'] or '2026-06-15' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any('screening' in c['detail'] and 'two business days' in c['detail'] and ('before closing' in c['detail'] or 'pre-closing' in c['detail'] or 'closing checklist' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The buyer's proposal shows $11,700,000 with seller support, but PF1 changes purchase_price_usd to exactly 11,400,000 and recourse_to_seller to false, while supplying the legal basis that must be cited.

The shared pool information gives no reserve amount, but PF2 changes first_loss_reserve_usd from a generic zero or unspecified amount to exactly 1,200,000 because the largest obligor is above the 10% threshold.
The draft does not specify the collection handoff, but PF3 changes lockbox_activation_date to exactly 2026-06-15 and requires the corresponding lockbox activation commitment.

Without PF4, a generic closing plan would omit enhanced screening and its timing, while PF4 changes enhanced_screening_required to true, sets the documentation deadline to exactly two days, and requires the pre-closing screening commitment.
